chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Is'haq ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Kharjah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Allah has assigned four thousand angels, dishevelled and dusty, to weep over him until the Day of Resurrection. So whoever visits him, recognizing his right, they will escort him until they bring him to his safe place; and if he is sick, they will visit him in the morning and evening; and if he dies, they will witness his funeral and seek forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.اسْتَغْفَرُوا لَهُ: They will seek forgiveness for him

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and angelic activities associated with visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the cosmic significance of Imam Al-Husayn’s (as) grave, where four thousand angels continuously weep, serving as a testament to his enduring spiritual presence. It emphasizes that Ziyarah is not merely a physical visit but an act of recognizing his divine rights (Haqq), resulting in tangible angelic services such as escorting the visitor, visiting the sick, and interceding for the deceased until the Day of Judgment.

en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim from Harun ibn Kharijah who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘Allah has assigned four thousand untidy and dusty angels to the grave of al-Husayn, Alayhi al-Salam. They weep for him until the Day of Judgment. They escort one who visits him with proper understanding of his rights, to his secure place. If he becomes ill these angels visit him mornings and evenings; and if he dies, these angels take part in his funeral and ask forgiveness for him until the Day of Judgment.”
